policy.locked_rule: Source attribution does not imply authenticity detection. Assign detection only when the paper explicitly performs and evaluates real-versus-generated discrimination as a substantive forensic task.
policy.guard: An N+1 classifier with a real class, model matching, unknown-generator rejection or real negative training samples alone does not establish a substantive authenticity task.

actions.title: Single-Model Attribution of Generative Models Through Final-Layer Inversion

canonical_identity.title: Single-Model Attribution of Generative Models Through Final-Layer Inversion

paper_identity_verification.title: Exact title matches PDF title metadata and rendered page 1.
paper_identity_verification.authors: Mike Laszkiewicz; Jonas Ricker; Johannes Lederer; Asja Fischer match canonical authors in order and rendered page 1.
paper_identity_verification.work_correspondence: The previously saved official PMLR volume listing links this exact mlresearch PDF for the same title and authors. Canonical record carries arXiv 2306.06210; no arXiv source was retrieved.
paper_identity_verification.version: PMLR 235 / ICML 2024 proceedings paper, 36 PDF pages including embedded appendices.
paper_identity_verification.date_note: Canonical year is 2023; the PDF identifies proceedings year 2024. Same-work identity is established by exact title/authors and the official source association. No publication metadata correction is proposed or applied.

actions.claimed_task: Open-world single-model attribution: decide whether an image came from a specified generator G. Section 2 also explicitly includes fake-versus-real discrimination within the framework.
actions.evaluated_decision_space: Binary +1 = target G, -1 = not G; experiments separately pair G with real images or another generator. Pairwise G-versus-real results are distinct from G-versus-G-prime attribution results. This is not an N+1 source classifier.
actions.real_image_role: Real CelebA/LSUN images provide negative training examples; real held-out images also appear as separately scored test comparators in Table 8. FFHQ real images are a test comparator for StyleGAN2 in Table 4. Some other experiments substitute another generator for unavailable real data.
actions.authenticity_formulation: The general decision concerns model membership, but the explicitly defined and separately scored real-comparator experiments instantiate generator-specific generated-versus-real discrimination. The anomaly score or real training data alone would not establish detection.

authenticity_evaluation.scope: Generator-specific binary real-versus-generated experiments within the attribution framework; no claim of a universal any-generator-versus-real detector.
authenticity_evaluation.protocol: Sections 5.1 and G.1-G.2 specify binary test accuracy, held-out target-model validation for the threshold, 1000 test examples per source in CelebA/LSUN, and five runs.

results.locator: Table 8, PDF page 34, FLIPAD/DCGAN row, Real columns
results.metric: binary classification accuracy percent, average over five runs

results.locator: Table 4, PDF page 8, Style-Based Models/real column
results.metric: StyleGAN2-versus-real binary classification accuracy percent, average over five runs

actions.source_attribution_evaluation: Section 5 and Tables 1-5 also evaluate target-versus-other-generator attribution, same-architecture/different-seed verification, perturbations and diffusion-version attribution. These comparisons are not themselves authenticity evidence.
actions.policy_reason: Retain detection because real-comparator binary tests are explicitly specified and separately quantified across models/datasets, not merely because real images occur in the data or a source-classification label set. Source attribution remains the primary framing; the detection support is bounded to the evaluated generator-specific authenticity comparisons.

confidence.reason: The real-versus-generated test results are unambiguous. Treating their systematic, separately reported binary evaluation as a substantive detection component is a policy interpretation; the paper primarily frames these experiments as single-model attribution.

evidence_locators.finding: Exact work/author identity and proceedings version.
Single-model attribution and explicit conceptual inclusion of fake/real discrimination.
Training labels and pairwise test protocol.
StyleGAN2 comparator set includes real FFHQ images.
Separately scored real comparator, distinct from generator/version comparators.
Dedicated Real columns for CelebA and LSUN; five-run means.

limitations: The main goal remains generator attribution; the finding does not imply a general authenticity detector across arbitrary generators.
No inference is drawn from related-work claims, real training negatives alone, or the word anomaly.
Appendices were included inside the same retrieved 36-page PDF; no separately linked supplement was retrieved.
actions.accepted_detection_limitation: Detection evidence is generator-specific real-versus-generated discrimination, not a demonstrated universal synthetic-image detector.

actions.title: Does a GAN Leave Distinct Model-Specific Fingerprints?

canonical_identity.title: Does a GAN Leave Distinct Model-Specific Fingerprints?

paper_identity_verification.title: Rendered PDF page 1 matches the canonical title after capitalization, line-break and typographic-ligature normalization.
paper_identity_verification.authors: Yuzhen Ding; Nupur Thakur; Baoxin Li match the canonical author list and rendered PDF page 1.
paper_identity_verification.work_correspondence: The official BMVA record explicitly redirects to the same paper path on bmva-archive.org.uk. That record gives the matching title, authors and DOI 10.5244/C.35.53, and directly links PDF 0197.pdf.
paper_identity_verification.version: BMVC 2021 main paper, 13 PDF pages (main text pages 1-10; references pages 11-13).
paper_identity_verification.redirect_assessment: The official BMVA HTML named the exact same-paper archive destination. Only that related official archive and its explicit Paper link were followed; the old virtual-conference first-pass URL and supplement link were not requested.

actions.claimed_task: Extract model-specific GAN fingerprint distributions and investigate their dependence on architecture, initialization, training dataset and transformations.
actions.evaluated_decision_space: Section 3 defines representations for groups of GAN-generated images. Sections 5.1-5.2 compare ProGAN, SNGAN, MMDGAN and CramerGAN fingerprints, seen/unseen initialization seeds, and unseen StyleGAN/StarGAN. The metrics are distribution similarity, not an authentic-versus-synthetic decision.
actions.real_image_role: CelebA images are bases for the added-sine-wave fingerprint simulation in Section 4. CelebA and LSUN supply underlying GAN datasets in Section 5. These uses do not form a scored authentic-image class in the main-paper experiments.
actions.authenticity_formulation: The introduction discusses binary fake-image detection as a related motivation/research line; the paper own formal task in Section 3 is GAN fingerprint representation and source association.

authenticity_evaluation.scope: No independently formulated and evaluated real-versus-generated task in the complete retrieved main paper.
authenticity_evaluation.evidence: Tables 1-3 and Sections 5.1-5.2 report Jensen-Shannon divergence/correlation for GAN fingerprints and their changes, without a real-image class, authenticity decision rule or real-versus-generated test metric.
authenticity_evaluation.limitation: The paper mentions separate supplemental experiments. That supplement was not retrieved, and no claim is made about its unseen contents.

actions.source_attribution_evaluation: Tables 1-2 use Jensen-Shannon divergence and correlation to compare fingerprints across GANs and initialization seeds, including unseen GANs/seeds. Table 3 studies transformed generated images; Section 5.2 also examines dataset dependence.
actions.policy_reason: The complete main paper supplies positive evidence for source-fingerprint attribution, while its formal task and all main-paper evaluations concern GAN sources rather than authenticity. Introductory motivation and real base/training images do not meet T1. Maintainer accepted removal of detection only; the authoritative task correction is applied.

confidence.T1_classification: high within the reviewed main-paper scope
confidence.reason: Formal task, experimental class space and all three results tables consistently concern generated-source fingerprints. No unsupported inference is made about the unreviewed supplement.

evidence_locators.finding: Identity; detection motivation distinguished from paper task.
Real images are simulation bases for added fingerprint patterns.
GANs, generated datasets and experimental setup; supplement boundary.
GAN/seed comparator identities and JSD/correlation measures.
Unseen seed/GAN comparisons and dataset dependence.
Transformations and overall fingerprint contribution; no authenticity metric.

limitations: No separate supplement, video, slides, code or third-party copy was retrieved.
Attribution-only finding is supported by the complete main paper and has been accepted by the maintainer.

resolution.accounting_basis: Final maintainer-accepted Wave 5A outcomes; ledger reconciled from Phase 1 plus finalized wave manifests. Exactly one authoritative task correction applied.
